children.title: DHS terminates Cyber Safety Review Board memberships
children.description_medium: Acting DHS Secretary Benjamine Huffman terminated current memberships on DHS advisory committees on January 20, 2025, including the Cyber Safety Review Board (CSRB). The board was then reviewing the Salt Typhoon telecommunications intrusions. The department action is distinct from CISA director Jen Easterly’s departure at the presidential transition.
children.description_long: On January 20, 2025, Acting Homeland Security Secretary Benjamine Huffman terminated current memberships on Department of Homeland Security advisory committees. The Cyber Safety Review Board was included. At the time, the board was reviewing the Salt Typhoon telecommunications intrusions. The supplied SANS account describes the memorandum and its effect on the board; TechTarget separately reports that CSRB members were dismissed. Together, these sources support an account of the department’s committee action and the board’s ongoing review. They do not establish that President Trump personally issued a combined order firing both the board and CISA Director Jen Easterly. Easterly’s departure at the presidential transition is a separate matter, not shown here as part of the DHS memorandum. The record therefore identifies the actor and action narrowly: DHS ended current advisory committee memberships, including CSRB membership. The evidence supplied does not establish that the review was formally halted or document what happened to its work afterward.
children.date_uncertainty: Jan. 20 is the memo/action date; cited accounts were published Jan. 24 and Jan. 27, 2025.

unresolved_components.title: Jen Easterly’s departure from CISA
unresolved_components.reason: The proposal says her tenure ended at the presidential transition but supplies no source URL or supported discrete event details for a complete child draft.
unresolved_components.missing_evidence: A source documenting date and circumstances of the departure and whether it was a firing or transition.

unresolved_components.title: Disposition of CSRB’s Salt Typhoon review
unresolved_components.reason: Evidence shows the board was reviewing Salt Typhoon when memberships ended, but does not establish that the review was formally halted or what happened afterward.
unresolved_components.missing_evidence: Evidence of the review’s status and disposition after the membership termination.

rationale: One supported DHS committee action is drafted. The proposed Easterly event lacks source support, and the evidence does not establish that CSRB’s review was halted.
